canDo: Fix the 3 most frequently recurring error types from Mock 1 with as little new content as possible.
review: Pick the Top 3 skills from the Error Book.
input: Short listening and reading that serve only these skills.
output: Rewrite the wrong sentences + apply them in context + redo them aloud.
checkpoint: Retest after 48 hours; only mark as “fairly stable” at ≥70%.
challenge: Today’s challenge: from your Error Book, pick the 3 kinds of mistake you make most often (e.g. passé composé / imparfait, misused connectors, unclear references) and do a matching set of exercises for each at Le Point du FLE; then rewrite 5 wrong sentences from your earlier essays and write a “personal rule” for each type (an explanation in your own language + one correct French example).

questions.why: The text uses contrasting sentences to show that piling up passé composé only produces a list, not a narrative.
Many candidates use it as if it meant « en fait ».
« Par ailleurs » only adds a parallel point.
The contrasting examples show the difference.
The rewritten example shows the concrete method.
The difference between « est-ce écrit ? » and « est-ce la réponse ? ».
Example: « il est tombé, il ne répondait plus ».

V42-01.exZh: The price is high. Indeed, the material is rare.

V42-02.zh: now, yet (introducing a fact contrary to expectation)
V42-02.exZh: This connector is very useful; yet it is almost never found in exam papers.

V42-03.exZh: It was raining, yet we went out.

V42-05.exZh: “Or” introduces a fact that goes against the reader’s expectation.

V42-06.exZh: This criterion is simple; however, it has a limit.

V42-08.exZh: Only one option answers the question asked.

V42-09.exZh: The reader must know what each pronoun refers to.

V42-10.exZh: To remove the ambiguity, repeat the noun instead of using a pronoun.

V42-11.exZh: If your answer isn’t among the options, reread the question.

V42-12.exZh: The choice of tense changes the meaning of the sentence.

V42-13.exZh: You need to practise hearing numbers in sequence.

V42-15.exZh: The word “comme” signals that it isn’t exact, which avoids a misunderstanding.

V42-16.exZh: A vague reference forces the reader to reread the sentence.

V42-17.zh: I’m looking for the word … (spoken repair)
V42-17.exZh: I’m looking for the word… the place where you buy medicine.

V42-19.exZh: I am writing to express my dissatisfaction with my order.

V42-20.exZh: I’m sorry, but this solution doesn’t quite suit me.

V42-21.exZh: You’re offering me a credit note, but I’d prefer an exchange.

V42-22.exZh: I do understand that time is short, but we need an answer.

V42-23.exZh: Set yourself a firm limit: half the text written by half the time.

V42-24.zh: one should distinguish X from Y
V42-24.exZh: One should distinguish a language error from a misreading of meaning.

V42-25.exZh: Before revising, make a precise diagnosis of your answer sheets.

V42-26.exZh: “En effet” confirms and explains what came before.

V42-27.exZh: Eight candidates out of twelve hand in a paper with a rushed ending.

V42-28.exZh: Listen to these numbers until they no longer need working out.

V42-29.exZh: You get the information across even without the exact word.

V42-30.exZh: This result is surprising given the situation.

V42-31.exZh: If your answer isn’t there, you misread the question.

V42-32.exZh: This option is true, but it’s off topic.

V42-33.exZh: Many learners avoid repeating themselves at all costs.

V42-34.exZh: Repeating the right word is almost always better.

V42-35.exZh: Get a friend to read your text before you hand it in.

V42-36.zh: to misread the meaning (get it backwards)
V42-36.exZh: With the wrong connector, you get the meaning backwards.

V42-37.exZh: The price goes up by fifteen euros; it doesn’t reach fifteen euros.

V42-38.exZh: I wrote to the manager, and the latter replied the next day.

V42-39.exZh: Authentic documents almost always repeat information.

V42-40.exZh: I’d advise you not to wait until the last day to send the document.

V42-41.zh: I would like to point out that …
V42-41.exZh: I would like to point out that I had confirmed my order in writing.

V42-42.exZh: The sentence is correct, but it doesn’t say anything precise.

V42-43.exZh: Half my mistakes are careless ones.

V42-44.exZh: Keep five minutes to reread your paper.

V42-45.zh: to keep X minutes for checking
V42-45.exZh: Keep five minutes for checking, without exception.
